newsitem.title: ITALY: Stefanel expects 16 bln lire loss for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Stefanel expects 16 bln lire loss for 1996.

text.p: Italian clothing company Stefanel made a small profit in the second half of 1996 and expected to end the whole year with losses of around 16 billion, chairman Giuseppe Stefanel said at a presentation.
The clothing group's objective for 1997 was "a solid and healthy break-even", he said.

"Definitive data will come next week but after a 1996 first half loss of 19 billion lire, I can say in advance the second half registered a profit of several billions and that 1996 will end with a loss of around 16 billion on a turnover of about 500 billion," Stefanel said.
After the expected break-even in 1997, "in 1998 we expect to start earning money," he added.
Managing director Gianfranco Cianci said debts in 1996 should fall to 155-160 billion lire from around 200 billion in 1995 and should improve further in 1997.
Stefanel made a consolidated loss of 69.4 billion in 1995 on a turnover of 575.6 billion.
Cianci said the group would have tried to return to profit in 1997 instead of aiming for break-even "but the solution for medium term development seemed to us not to pursue (profit this year)."
The group had already started reorganisation to improve profitability and "to reconstruct solid commercial and organisational bases for medium term business growth," he said.
This year recovery in turnover and the benefits of cutting non-strategic activities would become evident, he said.
Above all the company intended an organisational shake-up which should allow "higher gross margins with as low costs as possible," he said.
